text:
alex: FYI seeing a steady stream of apiserver 503s in eu-west1 since ~03:10 UTC. controller-manager queues are piling up, lots of backoff retries. looks tied to leader ejection events in etcd.
maria: on it — can you paste the apiserver logs around a spike? any deploys?
alex: no deploys. logs:```2026-03-20T03:11:02Z apiserver ERROR http2: server: error reading preface from client: read tcp 10.0.1.12:6443: connection reset by peer
2026-03-20T03:11:03Z apiserver 503 response write timeout```
hung: metrics: etcd_disk_commit_duration_seconds p90 jumped from 12ms -> 350ms at 03:09, raft leader changes: 6 in 3m. network RTT to etcd endpoints (peer network) spiking.
karen: also seeing a burst of watch event fanout from ksvc controllers at same time — watch-cache misses spike. controller-manager reconcile rate doubled.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-20260320-129 (controlplane ejection / apiserver 503s eu-west1) @oncall
maria: possible hypothesis: peer network flaps between etcd members causing leader elections, which amplifies commit latency, causing apiserver timeouts -> client retries -> controller queue growth -> more watch requests.
alex: can we temporarily reduce watch fanout? or increase apiserver replicas to absorb spikes?
hung: quick mitigations: 1) temporarily scale apiserver -> 5 -> runbook: run kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/apiserver --replicas=5 2) pin leader onto node with best network interfaces by setting etcd priority (manual leader transfer) 3) throttle noisy controllers (ksvc) by lowering burst QPS for them if possible.
karen: I put a short-lived admission patch to reduce watch cache TTL for ksvc for 2m to reduce chattiness (will revert).
maria: doing controlled `etcdctl move-leader` to node etcd-3 (lowest peer-latency). running now:```ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.0.2.3:2379 move-leader 3 --write-out=table```
alex: after move-leader, raft leader count dropped to 0 over 2m and etcd commit p90 back to ~20ms. apiserver 503s reduced. controller-manager queue is draining slowly.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: scaled apiserver from 3 -> 5 by @hung :heavy_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rollout completed: apiserver replicas 5/5.
hung: next steps: 1) run packet capture on peer network to find root cause 2) add extra monitoring alert for raft leader-flip-rate > 3/min 3) consider network QoS on controlplane VLAN in eu-west1 4) add automated leader transfer during sustained commit latency spikes.
karen: cost note: scaling apiserver to 5 is cheap short-term, but if this becomes frequent we need long-term infra changes (dedicated controlplane network or NIC upgrades). logging this on INC ticket.
maria: will keep the incident open until queues are back to baseline and no flips for 15m. tagging infra and networking.
alex: thanks. I'll follow up with logs + pcap on the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
